observation: Architecture critique Round 2 split-enforcement redesign was exemplary: identified undeliverable ESLint rule (6 false-positive sites), prescribed deliverable alternative (Date-receiver toLocale* ban), routed unprovable half to review + E2E. No rework needed — plan reflected critique and shipped production-ready.

E2E fixture reuse pattern (packages/web/e2e/fixtures.ts page.route LIFO override) worked cleanly. Architect prescribed pattern explicitly in plan task #8. Builder invoked pattern, zero hand-rolled harness. AC-1/AC-3 proof asserts hold.

TDD red phase (84 tests written before implementation) locked all ACs and edge cases (invalid/future/null/threshold boundaries). All tests green on first green-phase run. Zero test-writing debt at review.

Migration table was load-bearing. 17 sites + 6 exempt arithmetic sites enumerated + verified line-by-line. Builder executed migrations, grep sweep confirmed zero residual toLocale* calls. Completeness = 100%.

AC-1 proof initially incomplete: 3 surfaces (thread, knowledge, notification) captured; work-page surface absent despite spec naming 4 incl. work pages. Caught by code review as WARNING. Builder added surface-4 (WorkTask) in follow-up commit, closure cheap (2h). E2E/proof artifacts updated.

E2E assertions under-specified in initial run: AC-1 tests checked presence (not.toBeEmpty) not cross-surface agreement (expected labels matching). Proof screenshots manually confirmed 'all 14h'; E2E would pass with divergent labels. Builder later added .toBe(knowledgeLabel) cross-surface comparison. Pattern-catch for future AC-1 workpackages.

Session activity log 12h->24h normalization (site 15 behavior change) was intentional/in-scope but design artifact framed it as pure consolidation. Builder correctly documented in architecture and @lore. However, cost signal: register-purity claim in design artifact slightly overstated (R3 parameterized by both precision AND hour-cycle, not precision alone). Future time-formatting workpackages should nail down hour-cycle implications explicitly in design phase.

Pipeline cost: Phase 1 (designer sketch) minimal. Phase 2 (critique Round 1 found CRITICAL undeliverable, Round 2 redesigned + approved) = 2 rounds. Phase 3 (red: 84 tests, 1 session; green: 17 file migrations, 2 deletions, 1 E2E-mock-fix session; gap-closure: E2E mock-shape bugs + proof) = high iteration on mocks. Phase 4 (review: 1 WARNING coverage gap, 4 NOTES, DONE) = 29 tool uses (lowest phase). Total: 258 tool uses gap-closure session (E2E fixture shape mismatches), 215 in green session. Cost signal: E2E fixture mock-shape patterns deserve up-front specification.

Lore documentation effective: @lore AI3 comments captured name-swap deletion, killed-seconds register, 24h normalization, CommentRow carve-out. These are the four decisions a future agent needs. No filler.
